case_name: Khajamian Wakf Estates Etc v State of Madras and Another

State of Madras and Another
Supreme Court of India

facts: The judgment was delivered by K. S. Hegde, J.
The impugned Acts deal with agrarian reforms.
The Madras Inams (Assessment) Act, 1956 levied full assessment on all Inam lands except Warm inams granted on service tenure.
The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion Into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 provided for the repeal of the permanent settlement and the introduction of the ryotwari settlement in certain estates.
issues: Whether the material provisions in the impugned Acts are violative of Arts. 14, 19(1)(f) and 31 of the Constitution.
Whether the legislature had no competence to enact the provisions reducing the tenants' liability to pay the arrears of rent.
Whether Art. 31(A) protects a legislation where no compensation whatsoever has been provided for taking the 'estates'.
Whether the impugned Acts are outside the purview of Art. 31(A) insofar as they purport to acquire mining lands.
petitioner_arguments: The material provisions in the impugned Acts are violative of Arts. 14, 19(1)(f) and 31 of the Constitution.
The legislature had no competence to enact the provisions reducing the tenants' liability to pay the arrears of rent.
Art. 31(A) does not protect a legislation where no compensation whatsoever has been provided for taking the 'estates'.
The impugned Acts are outside the purview of Art. 31(A) insofar as they purport to acquire mining lands.
respondent_arguments: The impugned Acts are laws providing for the acquisition by the State of an 'estate' as contemplated by Art. 31(A).
They seek to abolish all intermediate holders and establish direct relationship between the Government and the occupants of the concerned lands.
The provisions relating to acquisition or the extinguishment of the rights of the intermediate holders fall within the protective wings of Art. 31(A).
court_reasoning: The impugned Acts are completely protected by Art. 31(A) of the Constitution which says that 'Notwithstanding anything contained in article 13, no law providing for- (a) the acquisition by the State of any estate or of any rights therein or the extinguishment or modification of any such rights....... shall be deemed to be void on the ground that it is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges any of the rights conferred by article 14, article 19 or art. 31.'

The expression 'estate' is defined in sub-Art. (2) of Art. 31(A). That definition includes not merely Inams but also land held under ryotwari settlement as well as land held or let for the purpose of agriculture or for purposes ancillary thereto, including waste land, forest land, land for pastures or site or buildings, and other structures occupied by the cultivators of land, agriculturists and village artisans.
holding: The impugned Acts are valid and protected by Art. 31(A) of the Constitution.
The provisions relating to acquisition or the extinguishment of the rights of the intermediate holders fall within the protective wings of Art. 31(A).
Art. 31(A) bars the plea that there was contravention of Art. 31(2) in making the acquisition in question.
